info.title: LoonFS Browser Proxy API
info.description: API for browser clients that access namespaces by alias.

get.description: Returns a summary of supported features and limits.
Returns committed changes after a sequence. A snapshot limits the feed to its captured sequence.

parameters.name: after_seq
parameters.description: Return committed changes after this sequence

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: End the feed at this snapshot's captured sequence

400.description: Invalid change cursor, limit, snapshot id, non-snapshot checkpoint, or after_seq above the snapshot sequence

409.description: The cursor is older than the retained change history and requires a fresh snapshot

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

post.description: Applies one commit: an ordered, non-empty list of path operations that commit together as one logical commit, under one commit id that makes retries idempotent. A single-operation call is the one-element case. The first operation that fails aborts the whole request, and a request carrying more than one operation names that operation's position in `details.operation_index`.

get.description: Returns the current file bytes, a retained revision, or the revision captured by a live snapshot.

parameters.name: revision_no
parameters.description: Optional prior revision number; cannot be combined with snapshot_id

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: Use the file revision captured by this snapshot

400.description: Invalid path, revision, snapshot id, non-snapshot checkpoint, or revision_no combined with snapshot_id

404.description: Namespace, path, revision, or snapshot not found

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

post.description: Authorizes one direct read of a file's content object and returns a short-lived presigned GET capability, the resolved revision, and the content reference the client checks the arriving bytes against. `Range` is outside the signature, so one grant serves ranged, resumed, and parallel reads. Deployments that cannot presign answer 501 `not_supported`; the proxied `GET /filesystem/content` route stays available and is capped by `download.max_content_bytes`.

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: Use the file revision captured by this snapshot

400.description: Invalid path, revision, snapshot id, non-snapshot checkpoint, or revision_no combined with snapshot_id

404.description: Namespace, path, revision, or snapshot not found

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

get.description: Lists a directory from the current state or a live snapshot.

parameters.name: include_attributes
parameters.description: Project each entry's attribute map and revision (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `false`: a page holds many entries and each map may be 64 KiB, so a listing does not carry them unless asked.

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: Use the directory state captured by this snapshot

400.description: Invalid path, limit, cursor, include_attributes, snapshot id, or non-snapshot checkpoint

404.description: Namespace, path, or snapshot not found

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

get.description: Returns path metadata from the current state or a live snapshot.

parameters.name: include_attributes
parameters.description: Project the inode's attribute map and revision (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `true`: a stat answers for one path and a map is capped at 64 KiB.

parameters.name: snapshot_id
parameters.description: Use the path state captured by this snapshot

400.description: Invalid path, include_attributes, snapshot id, or non-snapshot checkpoint

404.description: Namespace, path, or snapshot not found

410.description: Namespace deleted or snapshot released or expired

get.description: Resolves the current path to a file inode and returns revisions for that file. If the file could be renamed, use the inode revision API for stable identity.

Returns the namespace's recoverable deletions, oldest deletion first. Entries never age out at the retention floor; each carries the inode id and deletion sequence undelete needs, plus the deleted name when the delete recorded one.

Searches file content with a regular expression, accelerated by the namespace's grep index. Matches are verified against the real pattern and returned in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order; revisions committed after the index watermark are scanned exhaustively unless `allow_stale` skips them. Requires this deployment to serve grep and the namespace to carry a materialized active grep root.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Pattern in the Rust `regex` crate's dialect. Its UTF-8 encoding must be at most 1024 bytes.

parameters.name: path_prefix
parameters.description: Complete absolute path used to restrict matches.

parameters.name: allow_scan
parameters.description: Permit a capped exhaustive scan when the pattern has no required grams (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `false`.

parameters.name: allow_stale
parameters.description: Return indexed-only results when the unindexed tail exceeds the scan budget (`true` or `false`). Defaults to `false`.

400.description: Invalid pattern, cursor, or an unindexable pattern without allow_scan

500.description: The grep index is corrupt or its backing store is unavailable

501.description: This deployment does not serve grep queries, the grep index is not enabled, or its backfill has not completed on this namespace

get.description: Lists live snapshots in snapshot-id order. Released and expired snapshots are omitted.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, limit, or cursor

post.description: Creates a snapshot of the current namespace state. Every call creates a new snapshot.

400.description: Invalid namespace id, name, or ttl

post.description: Extends a live snapshot without passing its lifetime limit. Repeating the request has the same result.
Releases a snapshot by id. Repeated releases succeed.
Starts an upload session for content that may later be attached to a file. Service-proxied uploads send bytes through the server; direct-put uploads return object-store presigned credentials.

413.description: Body exceeds the 1 MiB upload-control limit

get.description: Returns an upload session. A completed session includes a new content token so the client can retry the commit without uploading the content again.

post.description: Ends an upload session without selecting content and deletes the object it was writing. Repeating it succeeds; a session that already completed cannot be aborted.
Completes an upload. The request mode must match the mode used to start the session. Direct uploads include a content claim; multipart also includes completed parts.

requestBody.description: The request mode must match the upload session.

413.description: Completion body exceeds the advertised `upload.completion_max_body_bytes` limit

put.description: Uploads bytes into a service-proxied upload session and returns the content reference for the stored object.

post.description: Returns one short-lived, checksum-bound upload capability per requested part of an open direct_multipart session. Asking again for a part is how a client retries it.

413.description: Body exceeds the 1 MiB upload-control limit

AbsolutePath.description: Validated complete absolute namespace path, serialized as a plain string.

ActorId.description: Opaque hosting-platform actor id: non-empty, at most 256 UTF-8 bytes, without leading or trailing whitespace or control characters.

ActorKind.description: The type of actor responsible for a commit.

ActorRef.description:
Identifies the user, service, or system responsible for a commit.

LoonFS stores this value as provided. It does not authenticate the actor or
look up profile information.

id.description: A stable identifier supplied by the application.

ApiError.description: HTTP error body used by LoonFS APIs.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason from the [`ErrorCode`](crate::ErrorCode)
registry.

Carried as a string so clients keep working when a newer server
introduces a code they do not know; use
[`ErrorCode::parse`](crate::ErrorCode::parse) for typed access.

details.description:
Structured context for the code, present when the failure carries
machine-usable identity (API spec, "Standard error contract"). Boxed
so the rare detailed error does not widen every error-carrying result.

feature.description:
For `not_supported` errors, the capability-document feature key the
client should reconcile against.

request_id.description:
Correlation id the server assigned to the failed request; the same
value is sent as the `x-request-id` response header.

AttributeKey.description:
Validated name of one inode attribute.

A key is 1 to 128 UTF-8 bytes and carries no Unicode control
character, which is also what rejects NUL. Keys are compared exactly:
nothing case-folds or normalizes them, so two spellings that differ in
any byte name two different attributes.

The `loonfs.` prefix is reserved for system-owned attributes. This
type accepts a reserved key, because a durable row has to be able to
carry a system attribute. The write operation is where a caller's
attempt to write a reserved key is rejected.

AttributeRevisionNo.description: Revision number for an inode's attributes. It starts at 0 and increases whenever the attribute map changes.

AttributeValue.description:
One validated attribute value.

A value is at most [`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_BYTES`] UTF-8 bytes. It is
otherwise free text: control characters and the empty string are legal.
Empty is a stored value, not a tombstone; only an explicit remove
operation deletes an attribute.

Attributes.description:
A validated attribute map for one inode.

Construction and decoding both enforce the same limits: a map holds at
most [`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_ENTRIES`] entries, each value is at most
[`MAX_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE_BYTES`] UTF-8 bytes, and the whole map is at most
[`MAX_ATTRIBUTES_TOTAL_BYTES`] logical UTF-8 bytes. The total counts key
bytes and value bytes and nothing else, so it does not depend on the
encoding the map is written in. Durable state that breaks a limit fails to
decode rather than decoding to something smaller.

An empty map is valid. It is the cleared state, and clearing an inode's
attributes is a real update with its own revision.

BeginDownloadRequest.description:
What a client names when it asks to read a file directly.

A path and, optionally, the revision it wants — the same two things the
proxied content read takes, so a caller switching transports changes
nothing about what it is asking for.

path.description: Absolute path of the file to read.

revision_no.description: Revision to read, or `None` for the path's current revision.

BeginDownloadResponse.description:
A short-lived capability to read one file's content object, plus
everything the reader needs to check what arrives.

The raw object key is deliberately not here, exactly as it is not in a
`direct_put` grant: a client learns a URL that expires, not an address it
can revisit.

The grant names one immutable content object, so it does not go stale
when the path moves on. A commit that replaces the file writes a new
object and leaves this one alone; what the capability reads is what the
requested revision held when the grant was issued, and the reference
says which bytes those are.

access.description: Short-lived read capability the client uses without learning the raw object key.

content_ref.description:
Identity, byte length, and checksum evidence for the object the
capability reads. A reader checks the bytes it receives against
`size_bytes` and recomputes `checksum.algorithm` over the complete
payload.

path.description: Absolute path as rendered from stored display names.

revision_no.description: Revision the capability reads, resolved from the request.

BeginUploadRequest.description:
Request to start an upload session, tagged by transport mode.

Each variant contains only fields valid for that transport, so invalid
combinations are rejected during decoding. The `mode` field is required.

BeginUploadResponse.description:
Response to starting an upload session, tagged by transport mode.

Each variant contains only the fields needed by that transport. Unknown
response fields are accepted for forward compatibility.

CapabilityDocument.description:
A deployment's self-description (API spec, "Capability discovery").

A remote client fetches this from `GET /v0/capabilities` and caches it; an
embedded engine exposes the same document as a constant. SDK gating logic
is therefore identical for both backends: check [`supports`] or
[`has_profile`], and treat a `not_supported` error as authoritative when
the two disagree.

[`supports`]: CapabilityDocument::supports
[`has_profile`]: CapabilityDocument::has_profile

features.description:
Named features and whether this deployment supports them. An absent
key means unsupported.

limits.description: Advisory numeric limits clients may use to pre-validate requests.

profiles.description:
Advertised profiles, each `plane/version`. All-or-nothing: every
required op of an advertised profile is implemented.

ChangeSeq.description: Sequence number assigned to a namespace commit. It determines the order in which commits become visible.

CheckpointId.description:
Durable checkpoint identifier.

A checkpoint is a durable bookmark to a namespace manifest version.

Checksum.description:
An algorithm and its canonical lowercase-hex checksum value.

The enclosing value defines which bytes the checksum covers.

value.description:
Lowercase hex of the raw checksum bytes.

The algorithm is its own field, so the value carries no prefix.
Provider APIs that report base64 are converted at the adapter.

ChecksumAlgorithm.description:
Supported checksum algorithms.

The enclosing value defines which bytes a checksum covers. Unknown
algorithms fail to decode because every in-memory `ChecksumAlgorithm` must
be recomputable by this build. Adding a variant also requires adding its
implementation.

CommitId.description:
Client-supplied idempotency key for one logical commit.

Reuse the same `CommitId` when retrying the same request. The accepted
grammar is 1 to 128 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores,
or hyphens, starting with a letter or digit. [`CommitId::generate`] returns
`c_<32 lowercase hex>`, but callers may supply any value in that grammar.

CommitRequest.description:
A request to commit one or more filesystem operations.

Operations run in order and either all succeed or none are committed. A
request with one operation uses the same fingerprint rules as a batch.

Unknown fields are rejected here for the same reason they are on
[`FilesystemOperation`]: the fields a typo can hide are the ones that
decide whether the commit is guarded at all.

actor.description: Actor responsible for the commit, as supplied by the application.

commit_id.description: Caller-supplied idempotency key for the whole request.

content_tokens.description:
Proofs for any new external content refs introduced by this request.
One proof covers every operation that names its content ref.

message.description:
Caller annotation recorded on the commit and reported by the change
feed. Part of the commit's identity: reusing `commit_id` with a
different message is a `commit_id_reuse_conflict`, exactly as it is
for an explicit commit.

operations.description:
Ordered operations to apply. Must be non-empty; they commit all
together or not at all.

CommitResponse.description:
Result of one commit.

Every commit resolves to this envelope — path-oriented operations and
explicit commits, embedded or remote. The commit id is the caller's
reconciliation handle: resubmitting the same request with the same id
replays this result instead of committing twice.

The response includes the same attribution and events as
[`CommittedChange`], including IDs created by the commit.

commit_id.description:
Idempotency key the commit landed under: caller-supplied, or
generated on the caller's behalf when the request carried none.

committed_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock stamp of the commit, in Unix milliseconds.
Observational: `committed_seq` is the order.

committed_by.description: Actor responsible for the commit, as supplied by the application.

committed_seq.description: Sequence number where the commit became visible.

events.description:
Semantic filesystem events in commit order. This is omitted only when
replaying a commit whose WAL history is no longer retained.

message.description:
Caller annotation, omitted when absent and carrying no filesystem
semantics.

CommittedChange.description: One committed change in namespace order.

commit_id.description: Client idempotency key for this logical commit.

committed_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock stamp of the commit, in Unix milliseconds.
Observational: `committed_seq` is the order.

committed_by.description: Actor responsible for the commit, as supplied by the application.

committed_seq.description: Namespace sequence for this logical commit.

events.description:
Semantic filesystem events for this commit, in the order the commit
applied them. One request operation may produce more than one event
(see [`FilesystemChange`]).

message.description: Caller annotation, omitted when absent and carrying no filesystem semantics.

CompleteUploadRequest.description:
Request to complete an upload session.

`mode` must match the mode used to start the session. Direct uploads
include the expected content details. Multipart also includes its parts.

CompletedUploadPart.description:
One uploaded part, as the client observed the provider accept it.

The server keeps no durable record of any part. Part bookkeeping is the
client's, exactly as it is in the provider's own multipart API, and this
is where the client hands it back.

checksum.description: Checksum the part was signed and accepted with.

etag.description: Entity tag the provider returned for the accepted part.

ContentId.description:
Durable identity of one immutable content object.

The body is 128 fully random bits, with no time component: content
object keys shard on the id's leading characters, and a clock-derived
prefix would put every upload in one window into one shard. The id
names *which object*, never what it contains — integrity evidence
rides [`crate::ContentRef`] beside it.

ContentRef.description:
Pointer to one immutable content object.

`content_id` is identity — *which* object — and the checksum is
evidence about its bytes. Separating the two is what lets the final
object key exist before the first byte is read.

A `ContentRef` is safe to publish only after the referenced bytes are
durable in the namespace's content store.

checksum.description: Mandatory checksum over the complete object.

content_id.description: Immutable identity of the referenced object.

kind.description: Content strategy used by the referenced object.

size_bytes.description: Complete byte length of the referenced content.

ContentToken.description: Proof that a specific `content_ref` may be used in a later commit.

token.description: Opaque, server-signed token. Clients must not parse it.

name.description: A label that does not need to be unique.

ttl_ms.description: Snapshot lifetime from the current server time, in milliseconds.

DeleteDirectoryBehavior.description: Directory delete behavior for path-oriented deletes.

DestinationBehavior.description: Destination-conflict behavior for path-oriented puts, moves, and copies.

DirectoryBinding.description: A directory entry's parent and name.

name_key.description: Name used to look up the entry.

parent_inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

DisplayName.description: User-facing spelling of one path component.

ErrorDetails.description:
Optional machine-readable details for an [`ApiError`].

Clients make retry decisions from the error code and use these fields for
relevant identifiers such as commit ids, writer epochs, and revisions.
Fields may be absent and clients must ignore fields they do not use.

active_acquired_at_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds at which the current epoch's acquirer took it, when
the head recorded one. Writer ids are process labels, so two runs on
one machine can share one; the stamp is what tells them apart.

active_writer.description:
Writer id recorded by the current epoch's acquirer, when the head
recorded one.

active_writer_epoch.description: Epoch that currently owns the namespace.

actual_attributes_revision_no.description: Attribute revision that is actually current for the inode.

actual_deletion_seq.description: Deletion generation actually active for the inode.

actual_head_seq.description:
Head sequence the namespace was actually at, which is what a caller
that still means to delete it retries against.

actual_revision_no.description: Revision that is actually current; absent when the inode has none.

after_seq.description: Change-feed cursor the request asked to resume after.

commit_id.description: Idempotency key of the commit the error concerns.

committed_fingerprint.description:
Semantic identity of the mutation that already landed under that
commit id, from the same receipt as `committed_seq` and present
exactly when it is. A retry recomputes this value from the request it
just made — see
[`put_retry_fingerprint`](crate::put_retry_fingerprint) — and equality
is what proves the two are the same request.

committed_seq.description:
Sequence at which that commit id already landed. Present when the
failure was decided against a durable commit receipt, which is what
holds the sequence; absent when nothing has committed under the id
yet and two live requests are simply claiming it at once.

expected_attributes_revision_no.description: Attribute revision the request expected to be current.

expected_deletion_seq.description: Deletion generation the undelete expected to be active.

expected_head_seq.description:
Head sequence a namespace delete required the namespace to still be
at.

expected_revision_no.description: Revision the request expected to be current.

fenced_writer_epoch.description: Epoch the failing writer session held when it was displaced.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

operation_index.description:
Position, in the request's operation list, of the operation that
failed. A commit applies all of its operations or none of them, so
this names the one that stopped the whole request.

retention_floor_seq.description: Oldest sequence still promised for incremental replay.

ExtendSnapshotRequest.description: Request to extend a read snapshot.

ttl_ms.description: Requested lifetime from the server's current time, in milliseconds.

committed_at_ms.description:
Wall-clock stamp of the commit that created this revision, in Unix
milliseconds. Observational: `committed_seq` is the order.

committed_by.description: Actor responsible for this revision, as supplied by the application.

committed_seq.description: Namespace sequence that created this revision.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

revision_no.description: Revision number within the file inode.

FilesystemChange.description:
One semantic filesystem change inside a commit.

A commit's events are the operations it applied, in the order it applied
them. One request operation can apply several: creating missing parent
directories, or replacing a file by moving over it, each produce an event
per directory created or file replaced. So a request with three
operations may report more than three events, and the events stay in
request order. Events name inodes and their parent-directory bindings
rather than full paths; a consumer that needs paths can stat the inode or
maintain its own binding projection from this feed.

FilesystemOperation.description:
One filesystem operation.

Unknown fields are rejected so a misspelled concurrency guard cannot be ignored.
Fieldless variants must use empty braces so serde rejects unexpected fields.

byte_offset.description: Byte offset of the match within the file.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

line.description: The matching line, truncated to the server's line cap.

line_number.description: One-based line number of the match.

path.description: The file's absolute path, derived at the snapshot.

revision_no.description: The matched revision (the newest visible one at the snapshot).

built_through_seq.description: Commits at or below this sequence were answered from the index.

head_seq.description:
Sequence this page was evaluated at. Pages are evaluated against
the namespace head at page time; the cursor is an ordering resume,
not a snapshot pin.

matches.description:
Matches in ascending `(inode_id, byte_offset)` order. A page may
return fewer matches than its limit and still carry a cursor: the
per-page verified-candidate budget bounds how much content one
request reads, whatever the plan's false-positive rate.

tail_scanned.description:
True when revisions after `built_through_seq` were scanned
exhaustively; false only when `allow_stale` skipped them.

after_seq.description: Exclusive cursor supplied by the caller, or the endpoint's initial position.

changes.description: Logical commits after `after_seq`, ordered by ascending namespace sequence.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose ordered commit stream was read.

next_after_seq.description: Cursor to request when another page remains, or `None` at `through_seq`.

through_seq.description: Snapshot head through which this page was evaluated.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence used for the read.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, if more revisions are available.

ListPathEntriesResponse.description:
One directory listing and the namespace head it was answered at.

The envelope names the listing target and head so an empty directory
still tells the caller which state it observed, and so the response can
grow without reshaping `entries`.

entries.description:
Directory entries for this page.

Entries are returned in canonical name-key order. Higher-level display
surfaces may sort entries separately for presentation.

head_seq.description: Namespace head sequence this listing was read from.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, if more entries remain.

path.description: Absolute path of the listed directory.

ListSnapshotsResponse.description: One page of live read snapshots.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page.

snapshots.description: Live snapshot records in ascending snapshot-id order.

ListTrashResponse.description: One trash listing page: the namespace's recoverable deletions.

head_seq.description: Head sequence this page was evaluated at.

NameKey.description:
Name-policy-derived directory entry key.

Use this for exact name preconditions. Keep user-facing spelling in
`DisplayName`.

NamespaceId.description:
Durable id for one namespace.

A namespace is one filesystem history. This id is not a display name and
should not be reused after destruction. Its serialized form is 1 to 128
lowercase ASCII letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens, starting
with a letter or digit; the `loonfs-` prefix is reserved for system use.

PathEntry.description:
Metadata for one path returned by stat and directory-listing operations.

File entries include the current revision and content details. Directory
entries do not. Attribute fields are included only when requested and are
serialized at the top level of the entry. Callers can pass
`attributes_revision_no` as `expected_attributes_revision_no` when updating
attributes.

ReleaseSnapshotResponse.description: Result of releasing a read snapshot.

RevisionNo.description: Revision number for a file's content. It increases whenever the content is replaced or restored.

SignUploadPartsRequest.description: Request for part-upload capabilities on an open multipart session.

parts.description:
Parts to authorize and the checksum for each part. Requesting a part
again replaces the previous upload for that part number.

SignUploadPartsResponse.description: Response carrying one capability per requested part.

namespace_id.description: Namespace that owns the upload session.

parts.description: Capabilities in the order the request asked for them.

access.description: Short-lived write capability for that part.

created_at_ms.description: Time the snapshot record was created, in Unix milliseconds.

expires_at_ms.description: When the snapshot lease expires, in Unix milliseconds.

head_seq.description: Namespace sequence captured by the snapshot.

namespace_id.description: Namespace whose state the snapshot captured.

TrashEntry.description:
One deletion that can still be restored.

`inode_id` and `deletion_seq` are sufficient to restore it. The removed
directory binding is included when available.

deleted_at_ms.description: Time of the deletion, in Unix milliseconds.

deleted_binding.description: Directory binding removed by the deletion, when available.

deletion_seq.description: Commit sequence that identifies this deletion.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

UploadContentClaim.description:
Size and checksum reported by the client for a complete payload.

Direct uploads provide this at completion. The server verifies it against
the object stored by the provider.

checksum.description: Whole-payload checksum in the algorithm required by this operation.

UploadContentResponse.description: Response after uploading bytes into a session.

content_ref.description: Digest and byte length computed from the accepted body.

namespace_id.description: Namespace that owns the upload session.

upload_id.description: Session into which the service staged these bytes.

UploadId.description: Durable id for one upload session.

UploadPartChecksumClaim.description:
One part's checksum, supplied by the client so the server can sign it
into that part's upload URL.

part_number.description: One-based part number, at most the provider's 10,000-part limit.

UploadSession.description: Current view of one upload session.

WriterEpoch.description: Counter used to reject writes from an older writer.

BeginUploadServiceProxied.description: Send the bytes to the service, which writes the content object.

BeginUploadDirectPut.description: Write the whole object through one presigned request.

size_bytes.description: Advisory byte length for an early provider-limit check.

BeginUploadDirectMultipart.description: Write the object in parts through presigned part uploads.

part_size_bytes.description:
Byte length of every part except the last. The server uses its
default when this is omitted.

BeginUploadResponseServiceProxied.description: The service will receive the bytes and write the content object.

namespace_id.description: Namespace authorized to consume the eventual staged content.

upload_id.description:
Durable session identity used by subsequent append and completion
calls.

BeginUploadResponseDirectPut.description: One presigned request writes the whole object.

access.description: Short-lived permission to write the object.

checksum_algorithm.description: Checksum algorithm the client must use for its completion claim.

namespace_id.description: Namespace authorized to consume the eventual staged content.

upload_id.description: Durable session identity used by subsequent completion calls.

BeginUploadResponseDirectMultipart.description: Presigned part uploads assemble the object.

checksum_algorithm.description: Checksum algorithm for every part and for the complete payload.

namespace_id.description: Namespace authorized to consume the eventual staged content.

part_size_bytes.description:
Byte length of every part except the last. At most 10,000 parts
may be uploaded, so this bounds the object at 10,000 times the
part size.

upload_id.description:
Durable session identity used by subsequent part-signing and
completion calls.

content.description: Expected length and checksum of the stored object.
Expected length and checksum of the assembled object.

parts.description: Uploaded parts in ascending part order.

binding_generation.description: Opaque identifier for the binding created by this event.

display_name.description: User-facing spelling of the new entry.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

parent_inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

FilesystemChangeFileCreated.description: A file and its first revision were created.

binding_generation.description: Opaque identifier for the binding created by this event.

display_name.description: User-facing spelling of the new entry.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

parent_inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

FilesystemChangeContentChanged.description:
A file received a new current revision — a put over an existing
file, or a revision restore (one durable fact for both).

content_ref.description: Immutable content published by the revision.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

revision_no.description: New monotonic position in that file's revision history.

FilesystemChangeMoved.description: An inode moved to a new parent directory or name.

binding_generation.description: Opaque identifier for the binding created by this event.

from_parent_inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

FilesystemOperationUndelete.description:
Restore a deleted file or subtree.

`inode_id` and `deletion_seq` identify one exact deletion. A stale
sequence returns `not_deleted` and cannot undo a later deletion.

deletion_seq.description: Observed deletion sequence, which prevents cancelling a newer tombstone generation.

inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

path.description:
Optional destination for the restored inode.

When absent, the inode is rebound to the parent and name recorded by the
deletion. Parent identity, rather than an old path string, keeps this
correct after ancestor renames. An explicit path is required when the
deletion recorded no binding.

source_revision_no.description: Existing historical revision whose content will be copied into a new current revision.

FilesystemOperationUpdateAttributes.description: Write and remove attributes on the inode one path resolves to.

expected_attributes_revision_no.description:
When set, the update applies only while the inode's attribute
revision is still this one. Absent means the update is applied
over whatever revision is current; either way the write carries
its own revision guard, so a concurrent update never merges
silently.

expected_inode_id.description: Stable inode ID within a namespace

path.description: Absolute path that must resolve to a visible file or directory.

remove.description:
Attribute keys to remove.

A list preserves duplicate entries so validation can report them instead
of silently deduplicating the request.

set.description:
Attributes to write. Each key replaces whatever the inode
currently holds under it; keys the inode holds and this map does
not name are left alone.

propertyNames.description:
Validated name of one inode attribute.

A key is 1 to 128 UTF-8 bytes and carries no Unicode control
character, which is also what rejects NUL. Keys are compared exactly:
nothing case-folds or normalizes them, so two spellings that differ in
any byte name two different attributes.

The `loonfs.` prefix is reserved for system-owned attributes. This
type accepts a reserved key, because a durable row has to be able to
carry a system attribute. The write operation is where a caller's
attempt to write a reserved key is rejected.

UnavailableResponse.description: The server cannot complete the request now. Inspect `code` to determine whether the cause is a deadline, shutdown, load, required maintenance, or invalid storage credentials. A mutation may still complete after a deadline or lost acknowledgment, so determine its outcome before retrying.

schema.description: HTTP error body used by LoonFS APIs.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason from the [`ErrorCode`](crate::ErrorCode)
registry.

Carried as a string so clients keep working when a newer server
introduces a code they do not know; use
[`ErrorCode::parse`](crate::ErrorCode::parse) for typed access.

details.description:
Structured context for the code, present when the failure carries
machine-usable identity (API spec, "Standard error contract"). Boxed
so the rare detailed error does not widen every error-carrying result.

feature.description:

client should reconcile against.

request_id.description:
Correlation id the server assigned to the failed request; the same
value is sent as the `x-request-id` response header.
